note: Missouri River bottomland south-west of Amazonia, on the river side of the levee. Two designated camping areas, each a bare gravel lot with no pads, tables, toilets or water: one where County Road 396 crosses the levee, the other about 1.4 km north along the levee road, at the end of a short spur about 100 m from the river bank. The river is hidden by bottomland timber at both. Open fires only in the designated camping areas. The ground is river bottom that floods. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: two designated camping areas (map symbols + GIS points), each at one of the area's two gravel lots - stays as designated points at lots. Free/FCFS/14 nights/no hookups confirmed. Not waterfront stands. Pin is on the north lot's gravel - no move. Phone matches. No split.
flags: DESIGNATED POINTS (lot rule - STAYS): page lists 'Individual Campsites' (and 'Boat-in along Missouri River'); brochure: 'Camping is permitted only in designated areas and is limited to 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period.' The 09/09 map legend has 'Primitive Camping Area' and draws two symbols, each directly beside one of the two Parking Lot symbols. GIS layer 27: two 'Primitive Camping Area' points, 39.86647,-94.93491 (north, the stored pin) and 39.85419,-94.93240 (south); layer 26: two lots, 39.86642,-94.93485 and 39.85475,-94.93289.

WHAT IS ON THE GROUND - NORTH (the pin): a gravel lot about 20 x 40 m at the end of a gravel spur that leaves the levee road and curves 150 m north-west; the GIS camping point is ON the gravel (8 m from the lot point). Timber on three sides, rough grass to the south. Nothing built. The Missouri River bank is about 100 m west and north-west through unbroken bottomland timber (leaf-on imagery; an estimate).

WHAT IS ON THE GROUND - SOUTH: a gravel lot about 20 x 55 m where County Road 396 comes over the levee and meets the levee road; the GIS camping point is 75 m south-east of the lot at the edge between a rough-grass field and the timber, with no pad or track to it. The restored chute is about 100 m south-west through timber. Nothing built.

WHICH IS MAIN: neither is built; they are alike. The directions on the page ('take Gravel Road 396 west 3 miles') arrive at the SOUTH lot; the north lot (the pin) is 1.4 km further along the gravel levee road and is the one whose GIS point sits on gravel and the one nearer the river. Pin left where it is; say if it should go to the arrival lot instead (39.85475,-94.93289).
NO SPLIT: the two points are 1.38 km apart but share one way in (CR 396 over the levee, then the area's levee road) and each is a single small lot.

ACCESS: County Road 396 and County Road 395 (gravel, county) across the bottoms, over the levee, then the area's gravel levee road; brochure: 'Motor vehicles are restricted to gravel parking areas and gravel roadways unless roadways are posted closed.' No ford, no posted limit, no 4WD wording.

FLOODING: both lots are on the river side of the levee (the map draws the Levee line east of both; the levee is visible on imagery east of each lot). Neither the page nor the brochure states a flood closure and the page carries no notice today; the note's 'floods' rests on the position inside the levee.
FIRES: brochure 'No open fires except in designated camping areas.' - in the note. Brochure also: 'Horses are prohibited.' (no horse camp).
WATERFRONT - NOT WATERFRONT STANDS: river about 100 m from the north lot and the chute about 100 m from the south lot, both behind timber, no open ground to the water and nothing to show a view.
PIN: stored pin = north GIS camping point, on the lot gravel. No move.
PHONE: stored 816-271-3100 matches the page's 'For more information call (816) 271-3100' (brochure: St Joseph Office 816-271-3100).
Page says 584.8 acres (map 584); the old note said 585. Nothing else in the database within 5 km.
